name: Proposal with how about
pattern: how about + NP, gerund-participial or licensed clause

entry.name: Proposal with how about
entry.pattern: how about + NP, gerund-participial or licensed clause

1.definition: Offers an item or course of action for consideration.

relatedConstructions.notes: How about a short break? and What about a short break? can both propose a break. What about the budget? can also take up an outstanding topic.
How about taking a break? proposes an option with a gerund-participial. Why not take a break? puts forward a proposal using a plain verbal predicate.

projection.target: The response can accept or reject the proposal. The phrase need not ask how a break would be carried out.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: How about a short break?
curious.summary: How about followed by a thing or an activity puts it forward as an option for the listener to consider.
curious.body: How about a short break? doesn't have to be a question about how a break would happen. It's a proposal: here's an option, what do you think? The listener can accept or reject it. How about can be followed by a noun phrase, or by an activity ending in -ing, as in How about taking a break? What about a short break? can propose the same thing, though What about the budget? can also bring up a topic that's still outstanding. Why not take a break? also proposes a break, using a plain verb.
curious.try: Next time you want to suggest an activity, try How about ... and notice how people answer.

teacher.summary: Gives learners a way to make a suggestion, with variants using a noun phrase or an -ing form.
teacher.explain: How about plus an NP, a gerund-participial or a licensed clause offers an item or course of action for consideration: How about a short break? The response can accept or reject the proposal. The phrase need not ask how a break would be carried out, so the phrase works as a proposal. What about a short break? can propose the same thing, but What about the budget? can also take up an outstanding topic. Why not take a break? proposes with a plain verbal predicate, while How about taking a break? uses a gerund-participial. This dictionary marks this analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: Gerund-participial is the CGEL-style label for the -ing clause after how about.

contrasts.note: Can take up an outstanding topic.

watch_for: A learner might read How about a short break? as asking in what way a break would be carried out.
A learner might treat How about taking a break? and Why not take a break? as the same form, when one uses -ing and the other a plain verb.
teacher.activity: Give pairs planning scenarios (a weekend, a lunch). One proposes with How about, and the partner accepts or rejects. They swap to Why not and notice the change in wording.

child.hook: How do you suggest something to a friend?
child.explain: How about can offer an idea. How about a short break? means maybe we could take one. Your friend can say yes or no.
child.play: Take turns suggesting things with How about. Your partner says yes or no. Try one with a thing and one with an -ing word.
